title: Hard Calls, Clear Notes
subtitle: The NP Casebook of Defensible Documentation
author: Dana Ellery
topic: Legally defensible documentation for nurse practitioners, worked case by case through the provider-level situations where an NP's note is most exposed.
audience: Nurse practitioners in their first years of practice, especially RNs who have just moved into the provider role and now sign their own H&Ps, progress notes, emergency and urgent-care visits and discharge notes. They know how to chart as nurses but were never taught how a provider note is read after a bad outcome; they work in hospital medicine, emergency and urgent care or primary care, and need answers they can find in the middle of a shift. Final-year NP students on clinical rotations can use it too; bedside RNs are not the reader.
promise: A defensible note for each hard call an NP makes: the differential, the abnormal result, the consultant who never comes, the capacity question, the patient leaving against medical advice, the discharge, the telehealth visit, the prescription. For every situation the reader sees what the record will be asked later, a weak note next to its defensible rewrite, and the short list of elements the note has to contain, so they can write, in their own words and in the time a shift allows, a note that shows what they saw, what they considered and why they decided. It does not make anyone lawsuit-proof: it makes their reasoning visible on the record.
tone: Precise, calm and practical: plain American English, legal terms defined the first time they appear, no fear-mongering and no war stories. Every principle is shown on a concrete note, each idea is explained once and cross-referenced rather than repeated, and the scenario chapters are built the same way so they can be found and used mid-shift.
